metadata.title: प्रधानमंत्री मोदी के 5 आदिवासी मंत्री | 5 Tribal ministers of Modi government | Main Bhi Bharat
metadata.description:
In the new Modi government, five ministers from tribal communities have been appointed, reflecting the administration's commitment to inclusive representation. Leading the group is Jual Oram from Odisha, the senior-most tribal leader in the current parliament. With his extensive experience and deep understanding of tribal issues, Oram has been entrusted with the significant portfolio of Tribal Affairs Minister. His appointment signals a strong focus on the welfare and development of tribal communities nationwide.

Accompanying Oram are four other distinguished ministers from tribal backgrounds, each assigned critical roles in the government. Shripad Naik, known for his dedication to public service, has been given a key role that leverages his experience and leadership skills. Durgadas Uikey brings to the table a wealth of knowledge about grassroots issues, ensuring that the voices of the underrepresented are heard and addressed. Savitri Thakur, with her background in social work, adds a compassionate and insightful perspective to the cabinet, enhancing the government's approach to social justice and empowerment. Lastly, Sarbanand Sonowal, whose dynamic leadership has been previously demonstrated in various capacities, continues to contribute significantly to the government's vision of development and progress.

The Modi government has made several promises to the tribal communities, including the establishment of an Eklavya Model Residential School (EMRS) in every tribal block and housing for each family of Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTG). These ministers bear the significant responsibility of ensuring that these promises are fulfilled, thus playing a crucial role in advancing the socio-economic development of India's tribal populations.
